mainProgression.description: The opening track of Dire Straits' historic 1978 debut album. Emerging from an atmospheric foghorn volume-swell intro into a driving, high-tempo B minor shuffle powered by Mark Knopfler's lightning-fast fingerstyle chicken-picking on a vintage red Stratocaster.

Driving 136 BPM shuffle featuring tight palm-muted bass notes and snappy treble double stops

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Cold, moody tonic minor establishing the gritty Newcastle riverbank atmosphere
A (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing rapid descending voice leading
G (bVI) - Submediant chord adding poignant weight to the downward motion
F#7 (V7) - Dominant seventh chord borrowed from B Harmonic Minor, creating intense resolution back to Bm
D (III) - Relative major tonic offering brief daylight during the chorus vocal hook

techniques.name: Fast Fingerstyle Chicken-Picking
techniques.description: Mark Knopfler's hallmark pub-rock chicken-picking technique. Alternating between the thumb on low bass strings and the index and middle fingers snapping treble strings upward with immediate palm dampening, creating a percussive 'cluck' impossible with a plectrum

notes: Rest the fleshy heel of the pick hand firmly on the bridge saddles for tight palm muting
Use the thumb for low root notes on strings 6 and 5
Snap the index and middle fingers upward under strings 3 and 2 for biting double stops
Incorporate ghost notes by lightly tapping strings against frets with relaxed fret-hand fingers
Keep the right wrist bouncy and supple at 136 BPM
sequence: Pick the low B root at fret 7 on string 6 with the thumb
Snap the double stop at fret 7 on strings 4 and 3 simultaneously with fingers 1 and 2
Dampen strings immediately with the palm heel for a crisp staccato pop
Execute the quick turnaround lick into the A chord smoothly
tips: Do not use a flatpick; direct flesh-and-nail contact is critical for the biting, woody snap
Select pickup switch position 2 (bridge + middle) on a Stratocaster for the signature out-of-phase quack
Practice the thumb-to-finger synchronization at 95 BPM before accelerating to album tempo

techniques.name: Volume Knob Swell Foghorn Atmospherics
techniques.description: Manipulating the guitar volume knob with the pinky finger of the pick hand to fade notes in after they are plucked, eliminating pick attack and producing ethereal foghorn effects

notes: Roll guitar volume down to 0 with the pick hand pinky
Strike the note or chord firmly with the thumb or index finger
Smoothly roll the volume knob up to 10 over half a second
Apply wide, slow horizontal wrist vibrato as the note blooms into sustain
sequence: Fret string 3 at fret 4 with index finger with volume at zero
Roll volume forward into singing sustain
Fade volume back down to zero before the next note strike
tips: A Stratocaster with low-friction pots is ideal for pinky volume swells
Pair with studio plate reverb and mild analog delay to simulate river mist and distance

sections.name: Atmospheric Foghorn Intro
sections.description: The song opens with distant maritime ambient effects. Knopfler uses delicate volume swells on his Stratocaster to mimic the sound of a foghorn echoing over the river Tyne.
notes: Strike the note with the volume knob at zero and roll up smoothly with your pinky
Add slow, expressive wrist vibrato as the note swells to peak volume
Let the note ring into the studio plate reverb decay
Listen for the subtle snare rim clicks that count into the rock riff

sections.name: Blistering Chicken-Picking Main Riff
sections.description: Pick Harris's snare snaps into life, and Knopfler launches into one of the most blistering, articulate fingerstyle rock riffs ever recorded.
notes: Thumb snaps low B root on fret 7, string 6, with palm dampening
Index and middle fingers pop the upper double stops with aggressive bite
Chop chords staccato to keep the rhythm tight and uncluttered
Lock directly into the fast 136 BPM driving shuffle pocket

sections.name: Verse 1 Newcastle Riverbank Groove
sections.description: Rhythm drops into a tight, stealthy groove beneath Knopfler's rapid-fire narrative lyrics, punctuated by staccato double-stop stabs.
sections.progression: Bm - A - G - F#7 - Bm - A - G - F#7
notes: Keep comping minimal and syncopated around the vocal lines
Use fret-hand muting to choke notes immediately after striking
Slide into chord stabs from one fret below for authentic pub-rock swagger
Emphasize the dominant F#7 chord leading back into Bm

sections.name: Chorus Maritime Drive
sections.description: The song lifts into D major for the title hook before cascading down through the Andalusian cadence with full-throated rhythm power.
sections.progression: D - A - G - F#7 - Bm - A - G - F#7
notes: Strum open D and A chords with bright, chiming projection
Step down cleanly through G and F#7 with authoritative downstrokes
Allow the open high E string to ring for extra acoustic chime
Feel the momentum build toward the impending guitar solo

sections.name: Knopfler Lightning Fingerstyle Solo
sections.description: The guitar clinic that launched Dire Straits' career. Knopfler delivers a masterclass in fingerstyle speed, precision, and blues phrasing on his clean vintage Stratocaster.
sections.progression: Bm - A - G - F#7 - Bm - A - G - F#7
notes: Execute rapid alternate plucking using thumb, index, and middle fingers
Bend the 9th fret G string a full whole step to F# with supporting fingers
Snap double stops at the 7th fret cleanly without sympathetic string buzz
Target the A# note over the F#7 chord for dramatic harmonic resolution
sections.exerciseLabel: B Minor Blistering Fingerstyle Lead Break

sections.name: Outro Riff Vamp & Tight Resolution
sections.description: The band locks into an unyielding 136 BPM shuffle. Knopfler weaves fiery blues licks between the driving chicken-picking riff before ending on a razor-sharp Bm chord choke.
notes: Maintain maximum pick-hand velocity through the extended vamp
Drop quick, biting blues curls into the spaces between chord hits
Lock directly with the driving bass guitar and ride cymbal
Conclude with an abrupt, tight staccato Bm choke on beat 1

guitar.recommended: 1961 Fender Stratocaster (Fiesta Red finish, maple/rosewood neck, vintage single-coil pickups)
guitar.pickup: 5-way switch in position 2 (bridge + middle) for the quintessential glassy out-of-phase Stratocaster quack

amp.recommended: 1970s Fender Twin Reverb / Vibrolux Reverb 40W combo with clean headroom

effects.distortion: Pristine clean tone with natural tube warmth; no overdrive pedal
effects.reverb: Studio plate reverb to simulate riverside ambient reflections
effects.other: Dan Armstrong Orange Squeezer compressor pedal plugged directly into guitar jack

beginner.title: Mastering the Descending Bm Cadence
steps: Learn the chord shapes for Bm, A, G, and F#7 in open and barre positions
Practice the Andalusian descending progression at a slow 90 BPM tempo
Work on clean fret-hand chord transitions without pausing
beginner.goals: Play the fundamental chord progression smoothly with steady timing

intermediate.title: Chicken-Picking Mechanics & Palm Muting
steps: Develop thumb and index finger separation for the alternating bass and chord pops
Master the fleshy palm mute on the bridge to produce the biting 'cluck' sound
Practice the main riff along with a metronome at 115, 125, and 136 BPM
intermediate.goals: Execute the signature chicken-picking riff at album tempo with authentic bite

advanced.title: The Knopfler Debut Fingerstyle Solo
steps: Master rapid three-finger alternate plucking on clean single-coil treble strings
Transcribe and perform the expressive bends, double stops, and blues curls in the solo
Integrate pinky volume knob swells during the atmospheric intro section
advanced.goals: Perform the entire 4-minute track note-for-note with master-level touch, timing, and tone

commonMistakes: Using a flatpick, which completely destroys the snappy, woody percussive bite of the chicken-picking attack
Letting bass strings ring out uncontrolled instead of maintaining a tight palm mute on the bridge saddle
Rushing the tempo; 136 BPM feels fast, so anchor your foot to the kick drum pulse
Playing volume swells too abruptly rather than rolling the volume knob smoothly with the pinky
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Pinky volume knob swell exercises on fret 7 of the G string
10 mins: Slow chicken-picking drills on Bm and A chords at 90, 110, and 136 BPM
10 mins: B minor pentatonic and blues scale double-stop articulation drills
15 mins: Full playthrough of the solo against the driving rhythm backing track
focusAreas: Thumb and finger independence using bare-finger chicken-picking attack
Clean, instant palm muting to produce the distinctive woody pop sound
Flawless intonation on whole-step bends at the 9th and 10th frets
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 100 BPM to lock in the thumb-bass and finger-snap coordination
Increase tempo by 6 BPM increments once 4 consecutive clean bars are achieved
Shift metronome clicks to beats 2 and 4 to internalize the driving pub-rock shuffle
